intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III (HHC3) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the AP2S1 gene (602242) on chromosome 19q13.32.

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III (HHC3) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the AP2S1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: This revealed the occurrence of 11 missense heterozygous mutations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of FHH3, that all affected Arg15

checks.claim: The AP2S1 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.32.
checks.evidence_quote: An analysis of SNVs within the 3.46Mbp interval on 19q13.3, which is the location of the FHH3 locus, and contains ~110 genes, revealed one SNV, a C to T transition in exon 2 of the AP2S1 gene
checks.explanation: Paper places AP2S1 at 19q13.3; the finer band 19q13.32 is standard cytogenetic nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is an autosomal dominant disorder of extracellular calcium homeostasis. It is characterized by lifelong hypercalcemia with inappropriately low urinary calcium excretion (Nesbit et al. (2013)). HHC3 is genetically distinct from HHC1, which Hannan et al. (2010) attributed to mutation in the calcium-sensing receptor gene (CASR). Nesbit et al. (2013) showed that HHC3 results from mutation in AP2S1, the sigma-2 subunit of adaptor protein-2, which has a role in endocytosis of the calcium-sensing receptor.

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is an autosomal dominant disorder of extracellular calcium homeostasis.
checks.evidence_quote: FHH3, together with FHH1 and FHH2 are genetically heterogenous autosomal dominant disorders of extracellular-calcium (Cao2+) homeostasis

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is characterized by lifelong hypercalcemia.
checks.evidence_quote: characterised by lifelong elevations of serum calcium concentrations with inappropriately low urinary calcium excretion

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type III is characterized by inappropriately low urinary calcium excretion.
checks.evidence_quote: characterised by lifelong elevations of serum calcium concentrations with inappropriately low urinary calcium excretion

checks.claim: HHC1 is caused by mutation in the calcium-sensing receptor gene (CASR).
checks.evidence_quote: FBHH1 is caused by mutations of a calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR), but the abnormalities underlying FBHH2 and FBHH3 are unknown.
checks.explanation: The paper states that FBHH1 is caused by CaSR mutations.

checks.claim: HHC3 results from mutation in AP2S1, the sigma-2 subunit of adaptor protein-2.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that missense mutations of AP2 σ subunit (AP2S1) affecting Arg15, which forms key contacts with dileucine-based motifs of CCV cargo proteins, result in familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type 3 (FHH3)

checks.evidence_quote: Thus, our studies demonstrate that AP2σ2 has a role in CaSR endocytosis as well as in the regulation of CaSR signaling via Cai2+

paragraphs.text: McMurtry et al. (1992) described a large kindred with familial benign (hypocalciuric) hypercalcemia. Affected members were hypercalcemic. Their serum immunoreactive PTH levels became supranormal by about age 30 years. Their serum inorganic phosphate levels were lower than those of unaffected kindred members. Some affected adults had radiographic changes suggestive of osteomalacia. The authors suggested that they might have observed an unusual variant of familial benign hypercalcemia.

checks.evidence_quote: A large kindred with familial benign hypercalcemia (FBH) is described

paragraphs.text: Lloyd et al. (1999) performed a genomewide search in an Oklahoma family with a variant of familial benign hypercalcemia (FBHOk). Linkage to chromosomes 3q and 19p had previously been excluded in this family. Lloyd et al. (1999) established linkage between the disorder and loci on chromosome 19q13.

checks.evidence_quote: we therefore performed a genomewide search, using chromosome-specific sets of microsatellite polymorphisms, in an Oklahoma family with an FBH variant (FBHOk)

paragraphs.text: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is genetically heterogeneous. Hannan et al. (2010) noted that HHC1 is caused by mutation in CASR on chromosome 3q21.1. Nesbit et al. (2013) noted that the HHC2 locus maps to chromosome 19p, and they showed that HHC3 is caused by mutation in AP2S1 on chromosome 19q13.3.

checks.claim: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Familial benign hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia (FBHH) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder that consists of three designated types, FBHH1, FBHH2 and FBHH3
checks.explanation: The paper describes FBHH as genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: HHC1 is caused by mutation in CASR.
checks.evidence_quote: FBHH1 is caused by mutations of a calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR), but the abnormalities underlying FBHH2 and FBHH3 are unknown.

checks.claim: The CASR gene is located on chromosome 3q21.1.
checks.evidence_quote: FBHH and NSHPT in most families is caused by loss-of-function mutations of the gene encoding the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) located on chromosome 3q21.1.
checks.explanation: The paper places CaSR on chromosome 3q21.1.

checks.claim: The HHC2 locus maps to chromosome 19p.
checks.evidence_quote: The loci for FHH1, FHH2, and FHH3 are located on chromosomes 3q21.1, 19p, and 19q13.3, respectively

checks.claim: HHC3 is caused by mutation in AP2S1.

checks.claim: The AP2S1 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.3.
checks.evidence_quote: An analysis of SNVs within the 3.46Mbp interval on 19q13.3, which is the location of the FHH3 locus, and contains ~110 genes, revealed one SNV, a C to T transition in exon 2 of the AP2S1 gene
checks.explanation: AP2S1 is located in the 19q13.3 interval.

paragraphs.text: Nesbit et al. (2013) studied the previously reported Oklahoma kindred and patients with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia in whom CASR mutations had not been detected. They identified heterozygous missense mutations in the AP2S1 gene that all affected the same residue, arg15 (R15C, R15H, and R15L). In vitro, the mutations decreased the sensitivity of cells expressing the calcium-sensing receptor to extracellular calcium and reduced receptor endocytosis. Nesbit et al. (2013) concluded that AP2-sigma-2 has a role in calcium-sensing receptor endocytosis and signaling, and that disruption of this role by the arg15 mutants results in HHC3.

checks.evidence_quote: Thirty-two family members (17 affected members and 15 unaffected members), from four generations, of the previously reported FHHOK kindred
checks.explanation: The paper refers only to the previously reported 'FHHOK' kindred and never spells out 'Oklahoma'.

checks.evidence_quote: In addition, 50 reported FHH patients (23 males and 27 females) in whom CASR mutations had not been detected, were investigated.
